name: FactorAlpha
short: An end-to-end quantitative stock recommendation platform: a data pipeline, a five-factor rating model, and the product API behind factoralpha.ai. Three tiers, 5,000+ US equities.
tags:
Python · FastAPI · Azure SQL
PostgreSQL · pandas · React
sub: A three-tier production system for rating US equities — cloud ETL into a warehouse, a multi-factor quant model, and an async product backend serving the live app.
role: Backend engineer across all three tiers — ingestion, modelling and the product API.
doc:
Overview

FactorAlpha rates US equities. A cloud pipeline ingests fundamentals, prices and analyst estimates for over 5,000 tickers; a five-factor model scores around 2,900 of them and grades each one from Strong Buy to Strong Sell; and an async API serves those ratings, fair-value analytics and portfolio tools to the live app.

What I did

  • Backend engineer across all three tiers — the data pipeline, the rating model and the product API.
  • The supporting pieces too: job orchestration, scheduling, monitoring and the release path.
  • A mix of data engineering, quantitative modelling and backend service work.

name: FinSight
short: The backend for a US equities and options trading app — order execution against a live brokerage, options analytics, portfolio monitoring, and the GenAI assistant on top.
sub: The Python backend for an algorithmic trading platform — 87 REST endpoints across 9 domain modules, wired to a live brokerage, plus the retrieval-augmented assistant.
role: Backend engineer — orders, market data, analytics and monitoring; built the GenAI core; led the runtime migration.
note: Client product, so there is no public URL — happy to walk through it on a call.
doc:
Overview

FinSight is an algorithmic trading platform, wired to a live brokerage. Orders, positions, market data, analytics and monitoring sit behind 87 REST endpoints, alongside a retrieval-augmented assistant that answers questions about the platform and a user's own activity.

What I did

  • Backend engineer on the platform — the REST services behind orders, market data, analytics and monitoring.
  • Built the retrieval-augmented assistant that sits alongside it.
  • Plus the supporting work: request validation, background jobs, and a runtime migration of the service.

name: Rule AI
short: A no-code business rules engine for credit decisioning — analysts draw decision logic, chain it into workflow graphs, simulate it in bulk and publish it as a secured API. I built the backend.
sub: A no-code decision-management platform for lending and credit risk: visual rule authoring compiled into executable workflow graphs, bulk-simulated and published as production decision APIs.
role: Backend engineer — rule compiler, workflow DAG engine, bulk execution, caching, access control and governance.
note: Client product, so there is no public URL — happy to walk through it on a call.
doc:
Overview

Rule AI lets lending and credit-risk teams write decision rules without writing code. Rules are authored visually, compiled into executable workflows, simulated in bulk against historical data, then published as production decision APIs. It cut client workflow time by more than 95%.

What I did

  • Backend engineer — rule compilation, workflow execution and the bulk-run path.
  • And the supporting layers around them: caching, access control and change history.
  • Built for a regulated setting, so decisions have to stay explainable after the fact.

name: corestrat.ai — backend + AI chatbot
short: Two production services behind the company website: the public chat backend API, and the retrieval-augmented GenAI engine that answers from Corestrat's own document corpus.
sub: Two production services live on corestrat.ai — a public FastAPI backend handling chat traffic, sessions and conversation persistence, and the RAG engine it delegates answers to.
role: Principal author of the current RAG engine — pipeline, retrieval chain, production prompt, service layer, config and deployment. On the backend API: performance, background-task persistence, engine integration and a live database migration.
doc:
Overview

Two services sit behind corestrat.ai: the public chat backend, and the retrieval-augmented engine it hands questions to. The engine answers from Corestrat's own documents at roughly 90% accuracy.

What I did

  • Principal author of the RAG engine — pipeline, retrieval, the production prompt and deployment.
  • On the chat backend, which the team had already scaffolded: performance work and the data layer.
  • Plus the supporting bits — background persistence, and a database migration run against the live service.

name: RawDiary
short: A journaling app with no login at all. Usernames resolve in the browser against a Bloom filter in under 10ms — no database call to check if a name is taken. Holds 100+ concurrent users.
sub: A stateless, zero-authentication journaling app. No accounts, no identity database, no sessions to keep.
role: Full stack, solo — the Next.js frontend, the FastAPI backend, caching, spatial queries, audio masking and deployment.
doc:
Overview

RawDiary is a journaling app with no accounts and no identity database. You pick a name and you write. Names resolve in the browser against a Bloom filter in under 10ms with no database call, feeds page out of Redis, and voice entries can be masked locally before they ever upload. It carries 100+ concurrent users.

What I did

  • Full stack, solo — frontend, backend, data layer and deploy.
  • Including the supporting work: caching, spatial queries, audio processing and hosting.

name: VeinChain
short: Logging in with the veins in your finger. We built the infrared capture hardware ourselves and put the identity record on Ethereum instead of in a database. Became two working apps and a written paper.
sub: Finger-vein biometric authentication with enrolment anchored on-chain, built on custom low-cost infrared capture hardware.
role: Smart contracts, backend, frontends and the capture hardware.
doc:
Overview

VeinChain authenticates a person by the vein pattern inside their finger. The infrared capture rig was built from low-cost parts, a ResNet model turns a captured frame into a feature signature, and only a hash of that signature is anchored on Ethereum — so there is no biometric store to breach. It became two working applications, and a paper we wrote up but never published.

What I did

  • Smart contracts, backend, the frontends and the capture hardware.
  • Spanned electronics and image processing at one end, contracts and applications at the other.
  • Evaluated it properly — 92.1% precision at 80.2% accuracy on our own captures, at the matching threshold the paper settles on.

A university project, built with classmates and supervised by a faculty member. The contracts, the backend and the capture pipeline were my part.

name: RAG-app
short: Ask questions about your own PDFs without anything leaving your laptop. LangChain pipeline running Llama 3 locally — zero API cost, and documents never travel.
sub: Retrieval-augmented question answering over your own documents, running entirely on your machine.
doc:
Overview

Ask questions about your own PDFs with nothing leaving your machine. A LangChain pipeline over Llama 3 running locally — no API key, no cost per question, and OCR so scanned documents work too.

What I did

  • Solo build — the pipeline, the API and the interface.
  • Local model serving, retrieval, and OCR for scanned documents.

name: EDU-AI
short: A learning platform that works out how you learn. A short survey infers VARK and MBTI style, a Random Forest classifier predicts it at 91% accuracy, and the material adapts to match.
sub: A personalised learning platform that infers how a student learns and reshapes the material to match.
role: Full stack — the Flask backend and MySQL data layer, the Random Forest classifier, the Gemini content generation and the interface.
doc:
Overview

EDU-AI works out how a student learns, then reshapes the material to match. A short survey infers VARK learning style and MBTI type, a Random Forest predicts it at 91% accuracy, and the content is regenerated in the format that suits.

What I did

  • The backend, the data layer, the classifier and the content generation.
  • Both sides of it — training the model, and building the application around it.

Built with three classmates. The backend, the classifier and the Gemini integration were mine.
